observation.visible_scene: A close, low-angle view of a dark, round cooking surface (a flat pan or griddle) on which two irregular patches of pale, foaming, bubble-textured substance sit. The left patch lies in the upper-left of the surface; the larger right patch occupies the center, with a small dark notch at its upper edge. In the blurred foreground at the bottom center rests a pale yellow stick-like object (consistent with a piece of butter). The background above the pan rim is a soft, out-of-focus light wall. The scene is dimly lit with shallow depth of field.
visible_changes: The two foam patches remain fixed in position throughout; they do not translate or merge.
Within the patches the bubble/foam texture subtly shifts frame to frame, indicating ongoing bubbling/simmering rather than a static state.
A small bright specular glint on the lower edge of the left patch flickers in intensity between frames.
The pale yellow foreground object stays in place and out of focus, with no visible motion.
The pan rim and background framing stay essentially constant, so the camera is largely static with at most negligible drift.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the foaming substance and of the yellow object is not confirmed by the clip.
The heat source and the start of melting/bubbling are not shown; the process is already underway at t=0.
Any later outcome (full melting, browning, addition of other ingredients) is outside the excerpt.
uncertain_details: Whether the foam edges expand or contract marginally is hard to confirm given the shallow focus and low contrast.
Any slight camera movement versus purely static framing cannot be fully separated without clearer background reference points.
